claims.meetings: Using the same approved requirements reduces coordination meetings.
claims.tracing: When requirements change, the team can identify the tests that must be rerun.
claims.approval: A human reviewer must approve each release.

scoreInstructionPrefix: How fully does the speaker affirm this claim:
scoreCriteria: Absent, contradicted, hypothetical, or only asked about
Related topic or partial statement without the full claim
The speaker affirms the entire claim, in their own words
The speaker affirms and illustrates the entire claim

meetings.instructions: What does the presenter report about shared requirements and meetings?

criteria.A: Adopting a common approved specification has cut the number of coordination meetings.
criteria.B: Meetings continue at the same rate or increase, or fewer meetings are only proposed.
criteria.C: No reduction in meetings attributed to shared requirements is reported; the speaker discusses something else or just mentions a common specification.

tracing.instructions: What does the presenter report about the effect of a requirements change on testing?

criteria.A: When a requirement changes the team knows exactly which tests need repeating.
criteria.B: The team cannot tell which tests to repeat, or the capability is only proposed.
criteria.C: No claim about identifying affected tests after requirement changes is made; a different matter is discussed.

approval.instructions: What does the presenter report about the release approval rule?

criteria.A: Every release must be signed off by a human before it ships.
criteria.B: Release approval is automatic, optional, or only proposed as a future policy.
criteria.C: Human approval of a release is not discussed; the speaker discusses a different matter.
